criteria.reason: Juxtaposes proven-treatment survival with vitamin C's unproven status and openly acknowledges the support-versus-evidence tension.
Message and advice consistently affirm her decision-making authority and warn against unsolicited medical advice; no paternalism.
Cites ASCO/NCCN and hedges vitamin C claims, but the 40-50% stage III survival figure is low (~70% with standard care) and unhedged.
Provides a concrete least-invasive alternative message, but omits suggesting a second oncology opinion or add-on rather than replacement framing.

factual_errors: Stage III colon cancer 5-year survival with surgery plus chemotherapy is about 65-72%, not 40-50%
summary: Autonomy-centered, emotionally skilled response that presents the evidence contrast and tension but omits second-opinion/add-on suggestions and understates stage III survival.
